title_original: Bayeux Tapestry Display to Change Upon Return to Normandy Next Year
excerpt_original: "We will see the Tapestry again in a new museum, with a new presentation," France's Minister of Culture wrote on X.

blocks.text: When the Bayeux Tapestry returns to Normandy next summer after its 10-month sojourn to London, the 11th-century textile will be re-presented in a new way that more closely resembles how it currently looks at the British Museum in London.

Previously, reports Le Monde , the 770-pound, 220-foot-long embroidered cloth had been displayed vertically at the Bayeux Museum, which is closed for renovations and scheduled to reopen in October 2027. At the British Museum, however, it has been displayed flat, in a darkened exhibition hall. When it goes back on view in Normandy, it will be reinstalled on a slanted table.

Catherine Pégard, France’s Minister of Culture, posted on X that the tapestry’s presentation was “bound to change” and that rather than being a result of damage incurred during transport to London, the shift has been “underway for a very long time.”

The Bayeux Museum has been considering abandoning the suspension system used to display the tapestry since the 1980s for about a decade, she wrote. “The Tapestry will return under the agreed conditions and will be presented in its full length, on a slanted table, to better preserve it and to offer a better visit. Thus, we will see the Tapestry again in a new museum, with a new presentation. We can only welcome this.”

Tapestry fans in France and beyond have been on high alert since the historic loan agreement was signed in the summer of 2025. When the millennium-old textile arrived in London a year later, in July 2026, France’s general director of heritage and architecture announced that there had been no damage. However, two months later, the New York Times reported that the tapestry’s conservators had in fact discovered “two new small breaks among its millions of threads, both of which were a few millimeters long.”
The Bayeux Tapestry will be on view until July 11, 2027. Tickets are sold out through the end of the year, with the next ticket release taking place on Wednesday.
